title: Affine full faithfulness for a perfect complex over a filtered colimit
statement: Let (A_i)_{i in I} be a filtered system of rings with colimit A, and let A_0 be one stage. Let E_0 and K_0 be bounded complexes of finite projective A_0-modules. Put E_i=E_0 tensor_{A_0} A_i, K_i=K_0 tensor_{A_0} A_i, E=E_0 tensor_{A_0} A, and K=K_0 tensor_{A_0} A. Then the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_{i \ge 0} \operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_i)}(E_i,K_i) \to \operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(E,K)$ is an isomorphism. Here $D(-)$ is the notion used in [def-pc-derived-category], and bounded finite-projective complexes are the affine form of [def-pc-perfect-complex].

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.29.2, Tag 09RE, affine case in the proof (bounded finite projective source and K-flat target)

proof.text: Replace the derived Hom groups by the zeroth cohomology of the ordinary Hom complexes Hom_{A_i}^\bullet(E_i,K_i) and Hom_A^\bullet(E,K). Each E_i is bounded above with projective terms, and each K_i is bounded below, so the one-point affine specialization [lem-sc-affine-projective-complex-derived-hom] identifies these ordinary Hom complexes with the derived Hom objects R Hom_{A_i}(E_i,K_i) and R Hom_A(E,K). On the one-point ringed site with structure ring R the global sections functor is the identity of R-modules, so H^0 of the point of an object of D(R) is the zeroth cohomology of any representing complex, and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] gives H^0(R Hom_R(L,M)) = Hom_{D(R)}(L,M); hence Hom_{D(A_i)}(E_i,K_i)=H^0(Hom_{A_i}^\bullet(E_i,K_i)) and Hom_{D(A)}(E,K)=H^0(Hom_A^\bullet(E,K)), compatibly with scalar extension. The bounded finite-projective complexes K_i are K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], so the displayed tensor complexes represent their derived scalar extensions.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.29.2, Tag 09RE, affine case

proof.text: In each degree n, the Hom complex is a finite product over the finitely many degrees p in which E_0^p is nonzero, of Hom_{A_i}(E_0^p\otimes_{A_0}A_i,K_0^{p+n}\otimes_{A_0}A_i). Each E_0^p and K_0^{p+n} is finite projective and hence finitely presented. The index set I carries the order i \le j used for the stages, and a filtered preordered set is a directed set, so (A_i) is a directed system of commutative rings as required by [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine]. That statement therefore says that every A-linear component map E^p\to K^{p+n} is the scalar extension of a map at one sufficiently late stage, and that two stage maps become equal at a later stage exactly when their scalar extensions to A agree. Since the differentials of the stage Hom complexes are the scalar extensions of those over A_0, the canonical map from the filtered colimit of the stage Hom complexes to Hom_A^\bullet(E,K) is an isomorphism degreewise and commutes with differentials.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.29.2, Tag 09RE, affine calculation

proof.text: For a filtered colimit of modules, a cycle in the colimit Hom complex is represented by a cycle at some stage: its differential is zero in the colimit, so the finite-presentation equality from Step 2 makes that differential zero after passing to a later stage. Likewise, two stage cycles have equal classes in the colimit exactly when their difference is the differential of a stage element after a later enlargement, again by the equality clause in Step 2. Thus the canonical degreewise isomorphism of Step 2 induces an isomorphism on zeroth cohomology, which is the asserted canonical map colim_i Hom_{D(A_i)}(E_i,K_i) ≅ Hom_{D(A)}(E,K).
